result.note: Official GDP release for FY2025–26: tested the headline and component growth figures, and the RBI's FY2026–27 projection.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about India's GDP data for FY2025–26, as reported in June 2026:
items: GDP grew 7.8% in the January–March 2026 quarter, and full-year growth was 7.7%.
Among the drivers cited, private investment grew faster than construction.
Agriculture grew faster than government expenditure.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Agriculture grew 3.6%, which is slower than the 4.9% contributed by government expenditure, so statement 3 is wrong. Private investment rose 10.8%, its fastest pace in roughly three years, ahead of construction at 8.4%.
questions.source: Agriculture recovered to 3.6% growth, supporting rural incomes.

questions.prompt: As of June 2026, what growth rate did the Reserve Bank of India project for the Indian economy in FY2026–27?
questions.explain: The RBI expects growth to slow to 6.6% in FY2026–27, down from 7.7% in FY2025–26. Inflation, elevated oil prices, geopolitical friction and monsoon risk cloud the outlook, and household consumption has yet to fully fire.
questions.source: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) sees growth slowing to 6.6% this fiscal year.
